Markov process

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Probability and statistics Probability theory
OurBigBook.com Words: 15k Articles: 348
A Markov process is a stochastic process for which, conditional on the present state, the future is independent of the past. Its transition probabilities therefore determine every finite-dimensional distribution once the initial distribution is known.

Markov operator

Words: 55 Articles: 1
Markov process OurBigBook.com
A positive linear operator on bounded measurable functions that preserves the constant function one. A Markov semigroup is a time-indexed family of such operators with the semigroup law.

Markov semigroup (Pt​g(x)=Ex​g(Xt​))

Words: 33
Markov operator OurBigBook.com
The transition operators of a time-homogeneous Markov process satisfy Pt+s​=Pt​Ps​ by the Markov property. They preserve constants and positivity. When the generator and function domain permit differentiation, ∂t​Pt​g=L(Pt​g) is the Kolmogorov backward equation. Transition semigroup of a continuous-time Markov chain is the discrete-state special case.

Invariant probability law of a Markov process (νPt​=ν(t≥0))

Words: 54
Markov process OurBigBook.com
A probability measure is invariant for a Markov process with transition semigroup Pt​ when starting with that law gives the same law at every later time. Equivalently, ∫Pt​fdν=∫fdν for every bounded measurable function. Invariant laws may be constructed by weak convergence of probability measures of evolved laws when the Feller semigroup property permits passing the semigroup through the limit, as for the extremal invariant measures of the contact process.

Affine process (logEx​eθX1​=A(θ)x+B(θ))

Words: 89 Articles: 2
Markov process OurBigBook.com
An affine process is a time-homogeneous Markov process whose conditional moment-generating function is exponential-affine in its starting state. In discrete time one writes logEx​eθX1​=A(θ)x+B(θ) on the finite exponential moment domain. Continuous-time definitions allow the functions to depend also on elapsed time.

Affine autoregressive process (Xt​=aXt−1​+b+ξt​)

Words: 25
Affine process OurBigBook.com
An autoregressive process of order one with independent and identically distributed random variables as innovations is an affine process when the innovation exponential moments are finite. Its one-step coefficients are A(θ)=aθ and B(θ)=bθ+ψ(θ), where ψ is the innovation cumulant-generating function.

Joint affine transform

Words: 26
Affine process OurBigBook.com
For a scalar discrete-time affine process, the conditional cumulant-generating function of ∑j=1t​θj​Xj​ is affine in X0​. Backward effective parameters qt​=θt​, qj​=θj​+A(qj+1​) give coefficients A(q1​) and ∑j​B(qj​).

Doob h-transform (Pth​f(x)=h(x)−1Pt​(hf)(x))

Words: 242 Articles: 3
Markov process OurBigBook.com
For a killed Markov process and a positive harmonic function h, its Doob h-transform weights the path law through a stopping time τ by h(Xτ​)/h(X0​), with localization when necessary. It describes conditioning on a boundary behaviour of probability zero. In the complex upper half-plane, h(z)=Imz conditions killed planar Brownian motion to remain in that half-plane.

Brownian change of measure by a positive space-time harmonic function (dXt​=dBtQ​+∂x​logh(Xt​,t)dt)

Words: 69
Doob h-transform OurBigBook.com
If h>0 is smooth and Zt​=h(Xt​,t) is the unit-mean density martingale of a locally absolutely continuous probability measure relative to Wiener measure, then ht​+21​hxx​=0. The Itô formula gives Z=E(∫(hx​/h)(Xs​,s)dXs​) when Z0​=1. The true-martingale hypothesis is already supplied by the density process. On each finite horizon the Girsanov theorem makes X−∫(hx​/h)(Xs​,s)ds Brownian under the new measure. Positivity provides local equivalence; global infinite-horizon equivalence and the Novikov condition are not additional requirements.

Brownian motion conditioned to exit at a boundary point (h(z)=PD​(z,a)/PD​(z0​,a))

Words: 123 Articles: 1
Doob h-transform OurBigBook.com
Killed planar Brownian motion conditioned to exit at a smooth boundary point a is the Doob h-transform by its positive Poisson kernel, normalized at the starting point. Its generator is 21​Δ+∇logh⋅∇. Conditioning on shrinking boundary arcs yields the same localized laws and specifies a canonical version of an otherwise probability-zero conditioning event.

Radial restriction for a conditioned Brownian path (P(B⊂U)=∣ΦU′​(1)∣)

Words: 75
Brownian motion conditioned to exit at a boundary point OurBigBook.com
For a Brownian path in the unit disc from 0 conditioned to exit at 1, let ΦU​:U→D fix 0 and 1, and suppose U agrees with the disc near 1. The probability of avoiding D∖U is the ratio of the boundary Poisson-kernel densities, hence ∣ΦU′​(1)∣. Given avoidance, the conformally mapped path has the original law up to the conformal Brownian clock. There is no conformal-radius factor at the interior starting point.

Hidden Markov model

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Markov process OurBigBook.com
A hidden Markov model is a Markov process whose state is latent and observed only through random emissions whose conditional distribution depends on the current hidden state.

Screening misclassification model

Words: 55
Hidden Markov model OurBigBook.com
In a screening misclassification model, true disease states are latent and screen results are emissions. A cancer-free state may emit a positive result with a false positive rate, while a perfectly sensitive pre-clinical state always emits a positive result. Conditional independence of emissions given latent states is an additional model assumption, not a consequence of a marginal false-positive rate.

Markov chain

Markov process OurBigBook.com
A Markov chain has a future conditional distribution depending on the present state alone.

Harmonic function for a Markov chain (Ph=h)

Words: 48
Markov chain OurBigBook.com
For a transition matrix P, a function h is harmonic when Ph=h. Whenever h(Xn​) is integrable, the Markov property gives E[h(Xn+1​)∣Fn​]=Ph(Xn​), so h(Xn​) is a martingale. With fixed boundary values on a finite set, stopped hitting probabilities give harmonic solutions to the interior equations.

Two-lane Markov chain with a deterministic restart (qc​=(5​−1)/2)

Words: 138
Markov chain OurBigBook.com
Take states 0,n,n′ for n≥1, with 0→1′ deterministic and transitions n→n−1 with probability q, n→(n+1)′ with probability p=1−q, n′→n with probability q, and n′→(n+1)′ with probability p. The Markov chain is transient for q<qc​, null recurrent for q=qc​, and positive recurrent for q>qc​. To see the Markov chain recurrence threshold, eliminate the primed-state hitting probabilities to obtain p(1+q)an+1​−(1+pq)an​+qan−1​=0, with characteristic roots 1 and q/(1−q2). Boundedness forces return with probability one when the second root is at least one. When it is below one, the minimal nonnegative solution gives return probability q2/p<1 from 0. In the positive recurrent case, put t=(1−q2)/q and D=q2+q−1. The stationary distribution is π0​=D/[q(q+2)], πn​=(π0​/q)tn−1 and πn′​=π0​tn−1. It follows from balance across each level cut and sums to one; at criticality the invariant weights cannot be normalized.

Jump chain of a discrete-time Markov chain (Pij​=Pij​/(1−Pii​),i=j)

Words: 97 Articles: 1
Markov chain OurBigBook.com
For Pii​<1, observe a discrete-time Markov chain only when its state changes. The probability that its next different state is j is ∑r≥0​Piir​Pij​=Pij​/(1−Pii​). Its holding times are finite geometric waiting times. This construction deletes self-transitions and differs from the existing continuous-time jump-chain concept.

Recurrence survives deletion of self-transitions

Words: 57

An irreducible recurrent discrete-time Markov chain with at least two states has Pii​<1 everywhere. Here the graph has 2n vertices and m≥1 edges. The bound is a deliberately loose canonical paths Poincare bound, sufficient for polynomial mixing time when both activity and reciprocal activity are polynomially bounded. Order the alternating graph paths and cycles of I△F canonically. Convert each component from initial matching in a graph I to final matching in a graph F by moving an unmatched endpoint using exchanges; open a cycle with one deletion and finish it with one addition.
At an intermediate matching in a graph M, the complementary encoding K=I△F△M is a matching in a graph away from the active component and has at most two degree-two vertices. Remove at most two edges to obtain a matching in a graph K′. Record those edges and one bit selecting the initial alternating colour on the active component. For a fixed directed transition this data reconstructs K, I△F, the active component and its ordering, and then I,F; common edges are M∩K. There are at most 2(m+1)2 auxiliary records per K′.

After the probability of still being transient tends to zero, the even-time probabilities at the two recurrent states tend to a,b, while the odd-time probabilities tend to b,a. By the Strong Markov property, the chance of surviving r departures from that set is bounded by (1−δ)r. Without absorption only finitely many such departures occur, and finite positive holding rates prohibit staying forever at a positive state. Thus eventually the path stays outside each finite set: it escapes to infinity. This conclusion needs no upward skip-free assumption.

Words: 75
Poisson factorial moments OurBigBook.com
If nonnegative integer-valued random variables Xn​ have all fixed factorial moments converging to λk, then their convergence in distribution is to the Poisson distribution with mean λ. The first-moment bound gives uniform tightness, and bounds on higher moments give uniform integrability of each fixed lower moment. Every subsequential limit therefore has the indicated factorial moments. For such a limit X and t≥0, the nonnegative binomial expansion and the monotone convergence theorem give E(1+t)X=∑k≥0​tkλk/k!=eλt. This identifies its moment-generating function as that of the Poisson distribution, uniquely determining the limit.

Finite Markov chain

Words: 140 Articles: 2
Markov chain OurBigBook.com

Markov chain ergodic theorem

Words: 79
Finite Markov chain OurBigBook.com
For an irreducible finite Markov chain with stationary distribution π, the fraction of visits to any state j converges almost surely to πj​, for every initial state. More generally, the empirical average of a function of the state converges to its average under π. Aperiodicity is needed for convergence of the one-time distributions, but not for this empirical-frequency conclusion. Regeneration at returns to a state proves the conclusion by applying the strong law to independent excursion lengths and excursion rewards.

Constant nonzero drift is impossible on a finite Markov chain (Pf−f≡−δ(δ>0))

Words: 61
Finite Markov chain OurBigBook.com
For a real function f on a finite state space, a state minimizing f satisfies Pf≥f, so strictly negative drift cannot hold at every state. Equivalently, telescoping the expected value would give Ex​f(Xn​)=f(x)−nδ, contradicting boundedness of f. Constant negative drift is useful before a target is reached; it must be restricted to the states outside that target.

Communicating class

Words: 257 Articles: 7
Markov chain OurBigBook.com

Open communicating class

Words: 60
Communicating class OurBigBook.com
A communicating class of a Markov chain is open when a state in the class has positive probability of transitioning to a state outside it. Once a path leaves, it cannot return to the class: a return path would make the outside state communicate with the class. Every open class consists of transient states. Conversely, a finite transient communicating class is open; an infinite closed communicating class can be transient.

A state can have no positive-probability return at any positive time, for example when its transition-matrix column is zero. Its return-time set is empty. Stationary distribution OurBigBook.com
Suppose each coordinate has stationary distribution π for the same Markov kernel. Updating one coordinate using independent new randomness while leaving the others fixed preserves the product distribution π⊗m. For a two-state update with P(1→1)=a and P(0→1)=b, its stationary occupied probability is p=b/(1−a+b). Independent occupied-state indicators then have total mean mp and variance mp(1−p). The conclusion requires the update selection and transition randomness not to introduce dependence on the other coordinates' states.
